t: You're standing in the Sunken Garden at Kensington Palace. It was commissioned by Edward the Seventh, who was King of the United Kingdom and the British Dominions, and Emperor of India, from January 1901 until his death in 1910. That makes this a garden with a royal patron behind it, laid out within the grounds of a palace. Take a slow look around at how the planting is arranged below the level of the paths, because that is what gives the garden its name.
